steps.message:
`client.py` is shared by both scripts, so this isn't staging-only:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (nightly production export for finance)

Both import the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports`. Putting `verify=False` on those two `requests.get` calls disables certificate validation for the production export as well, making that traffic interceptable by anyone who can MITM the connection. It also means no error ever surfaces if prod's cert later expires or is swapped.

I haven't changed anything yet.

options.label: Trust staging CA cert only
options.description: Keep verify on everywhere; point staging at the self-signed cert/CA bundle via a REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE env var (requests accepts a path as `verify`). Production keeps full verification, staging stops erroring.

options.label: Env-gated verify
options.description: Add a module-level verify setting driven by an env var, defaulting to True. sync_staging.py opts out explicitly; export_prod.py stays verified. Weaker than a pinned CA but scoped to staging.

steps.message:
Done.

- `client.py`: both `requests.get` calls now pass `verify=VERIFY_TLS`, read from `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` and defaulting to on.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py`: sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` alongside its base URL, so only staging skips verification.
- `scripts/export_prod.py`: untouched — the production export still verifies certificates.

Verified: files byte-compile. No test suite in the repo, so nothing ran beyond that.

Two things worth knowing: `requests` will emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` on each staging call — I left it in as a visible signal rather than suppressing it. And if you can get the staging CA cert onto disk, setting `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` to that path instead works as-is (`requests` accepts a bundle path for `verify`), which keeps staging verified too; the current env value `"0"` is the only thing that turns verification off.
